[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This guidance provides a single-page entry point for authors who need to create AI coding assistant constructs (Skills, Agents, Commands, Prompts, Rules, Instructions). It routes authors to the correct standards and guidance documents based on what they are trying to create, and provides a minimal checklist for each construct type so teams can begin authoring immediately without reading the full corpus of 13+ documents.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#business-value]

### Business Value

- **Reduced onboarding time** — Authors find the right documents in seconds rather than navigating the full artifact hierarchy
- **Fewer authoring errors** — Checklists surface mandatory requirements before PR submission
- **Cross-team consistency** — All authors follow the same decision path regardless of which team they belong to
- **Reduced review burden** — EA reviewers see fewer PRs rejected for structural violations

#### Current State Assessment

The enterprise AI authoring framework comprises:
- 1 taxonomy ADR ([ADR-TEC-020](../../../../decisions/technology/ADR-TEC-020-ai-coding-assistant-construct-taxonomy.md))
- 6 mandatory standards (STD-TEC-AI-001 through STD-TEC-AI-006)
- 7 implementation guidance documents (GUID-TECH-IMPL-005 through GUID-TECH-IMPL-011)
- 2 reusable patterns (PTN-TEC-AI-003, PTN-TEC-AI-004)

Authors need a way to navigate this corpus efficiently.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#problem-description]

#### Problem Description

Authors face a "wall of documents" with no clear entry point. The taxonomy ADR defines constructs conceptually but doesn't tell an author which files to create or which guidance to read. The standards define mandatory requirements but assume familiarity with the construct model. The guidance documents are comprehensive but construct-specific — an author must already know their construct type to select the right document.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#principle-1-route-first-read-second]

#### Principle 1: Route First, Read Second

**Description:** Always determine which construct type you need before reading detailed guidance.
**Rationale:** Reading the wrong guidance document wastes time and creates confusion.
**Application:** Use the [Construct Selection Decision Tree](#construct-selection-decision-tree) below before opening any other document.
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#principle-2-minimum-viable-conformance]

#### Principle 2: Minimum Viable Conformance

**Description:** Meet all mandatory requirements (MRs) from the governing standard before adding optional enhancements.
**Rationale:** Standards define the floor — guidance documents show the ceiling. Get the floor right first.
**Application:** Use the [Per-Construct Checklists](#per-construct-checklists) to verify mandatory requirements before submitting a PR.
page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#principle-3-name-it-right-the-first-time]

#### Principle 3: Name It Right the First Time

**Description:** Follow naming conventions from the start — renaming constructs after adoption is expensive.
**Rationale:** Construct names become invocation commands, file paths, and cross-references. Changing them breaks all consumers.
**Application:** Check the naming table in the relevant guidance document before creating any file.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#construct-selection-decision-tree]

### Construct Selection Decision Tree

Use this decision tree to determine which construct type to create:

```
What are you trying to accomplish?
│
├── Define reusable domain expertise that multiple workflows invoke
│   └── CREATE A SKILL → Read STD-001 + GUID-009
│
├── Create an autonomous entity that owns a scope and composes Skills
│   └── CREATE AN AGENT → Read STD-002 + GUID-010
│
├── Define a multi-step workflow triggered by a user
│   ├── For Claude Code?
│   │   └── CREATE A COMMAND → Read STD-004 + GUID-006
│   ├── For GitHub Copilot?
│   │   └── CREATE A PROMPT → Read STD-004 + GUID-007
│   └── For both? (most common)
│       └── CREATE COMMAND + PROMPT PAIR → Read STD-004 + GUID-006 + GUID-007 + PTN-003
│
├── Set behavioral constraints scoped to specific file patterns
│   └── CREATE A RULE → Read STD-005 + GUID-008
│
├── Define repository-wide context and conventions
│   └── UPDATE INSTRUCTION FILES → Read STD-003 + PTN-003
│
└── Unsure / My intent doesn't fit any of the above
    └── READ THE TAXONOMY → ADR-TEC-020 + GUID-005
```

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#naming-quick-reference]

### Naming Quick-Reference

| Construct | Convention | Location | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Skill directory | kebab-case noun or role-noun | `.claude/skills/<name>/` | `business-analyst`, `tech-evaluator` |
| Skill file | Always `SKILL.md` | `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | `SKILL.md` |
| Agent file | `<function>.agent.md` | `.github/agents/` | `ea-reviewer.agent.md` |
| Command file | `eap-[<phase>-]<noun>[-<verb>].md` (bootstrap-derived); unprefixed `<noun>[-<verb>].md` for Commands unique to this repository | `.claude/commands/` | `pr-appr-review.md`; `adr.md`, `activity-brief.md` (ref-arch-unique) |
| Prompt file | Same as command + `.prompt.md` | `.github/prompts/` | `pr-appr-review.prompt.md`; `adr.prompt.md`, `activity-brief.prompt.md` (ref-arch-unique) |
| Rule file (Claude) | kebab-case concern + `.md` | `.claude/rules/` | `drawio.md`, `terraform.md` |
| Rule file (Copilot) | kebab-case concern + `.instructions.md` | `.github/instructions/` | `drawio.instructions.md` |
| Instruction file (Claude) | `CLAUDE.md` | Repository root | `CLAUDE.md` |
| Instruction file (Copilot) | `copilot-instructions.md` | `.github/` | `copilot-instructions.md` |
| Autonomous context | `AGENTS.md` | Repository root | `AGENTS.md` |

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#pitfall-1-creating-a-skill-when-you-need-a-command]

#### Pitfall 1: Creating a Skill When You Need a Command

**Description:** Authors encode a multi-step workflow (lint → test → push) as a Skill instead of a Command that invokes Skills.
**Impact:** Skills become procedural scripts rather than reusable expertise. Other Commands cannot compose them.
**Prevention:** If your construct has sequential steps with tool invocations, it's a Command. If it defines *what to know* rather than *what to do*, it's a Skill.
**Mitigation:** Refactor into a Command that references the relevant Skills for domain knowledge.
page_texts.30:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#pitfall-2-creating-a-rule-when-you-need-a-skill]

#### Pitfall 2: Creating a Rule When You Need a Skill

**Description:** Authors write 50+ lines of behavioral guidance as a rule file.
**Impact:** Rule files are designed for brief constraints (5–20 lines). Long rules bloat context windows and reduce agent performance.
**Prevention:** If the content exceeds 20 lines or defines a workflow, create a Skill instead.
**Mitigation:** Extract the content into `.claude/skills/<concern>/SKILL.md` and reduce the rule to a 2-line pointer.
page_texts.31:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#pitfall-3-forgetting-cross-tool-synchronization]

#### Pitfall 3: Forgetting Cross-Tool Synchronization

**Description:** Author creates a Claude Command but not the corresponding Copilot Prompt (or vice versa).
**Impact:** Teams using the other tool have no equivalent workflow, creating capability drift.
**Prevention:** Always create both: Command (`.claude/commands/<name>.md`) + Prompt (`.github/prompts/<name>.prompt.md`). See [PTN-TEC-AI-003](../../../../patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md).
**Mitigation:** Run the `/eap-ai-sync` workflow to identify desynchronized constructs.
page_texts.32:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#pitfall-4-using-the-wrong-frontmatter-key]

#### Pitfall 4: Using the Wrong Frontmatter Key

**Description:** Author uses `globs:` or `applyTo:` in a Claude rule file (should be `paths:`), or uses `paths:` in a Copilot instruction (should be `applyTo:`).
**Impact:** The construct silently fails to activate — the tool ignores unrecognized keys.
**Prevention:** Claude uses `paths:` (YAML list). Copilot uses `applyTo:` (comma-separated string). See [STD-TEC-AI-005 MR-2](../../../../standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-005-file-pattern-instruction.md).
**Mitigation:** Validate frontmatter keys before committing.
page_texts.35:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#methodology-overview]

#### Methodology Overview

This quick-start uses a **select → scaffold → validate → sync** methodology: pick the construct type, create files from the template, validate against the checklist, then synchronize cross-tool equivalents.
page_texts.36:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#implementation-lifecycle]

| Phase | Objectives | Key Activities | Deliverables |

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#skill-checklist]

#### Skill Checklist

- [ ] Directory created at `.claude/skills/<kebab-case-name>/`
- [ ] File named `SKILL.md` (uppercase)
- [ ] YAML frontmatter with `name:` and `description:` (≤ 300 chars)
- [ ] Operating instruction (single imperative sentence after frontmatter)
- [ ] `## Scope` section with boundaries
- [ ] `## Workflow` section with numbered steps
- [ ] `## Guidelines` section with ownership and delegation rules
- [ ] Single-responsibility: Skill covers one bounded domain
- [ ] No tool invocations in the Skill (those belong in Commands)
- [ ] Referenced in relevant Command(s) that consume this Skill

**Governing documents:** [STD-TEC-AI-001](../../../../standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-001-skill-authoring.md) • [GUID-TECH-IMPL-009](./GUID-TECH-IMPL-009-skill-authoring-guidance.md)
page_texts.39:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#agent-checklist]

#### Agent Checklist

- [ ] File created at `.github/agents/<function>.agent.md`
- [ ] YAML frontmatter with `description:` (≤ 500 chars) and `tools:` array
- [ ] Tools follow least-privilege (only what the agent needs)
- [ ] `## Rules` section with behavioral constraints
- [ ] `## Conventions` section referencing `AGENTS.md` for build commands
- [ ] Ownership matrix defined (what files this agent may/must not modify)
- [ ] Skills referenced by path (`.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`)
- [ ] Does not overlap scope with existing agents

**Governing documents:** [STD-TEC-AI-002](../../../../standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-002-agent-definition.md) • [GUID-TECH-IMPL-010](./GUID-TECH-IMPL-010-agent-authoring-guidance.md)
page_texts.40:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#command--prompt-pair-checklist]

#### Command + Prompt Pair Checklist

- [ ] Command file at `.claude/commands/<verb-or-verb-noun>.md`
- [ ] Prompt file at `.github/prompts/<same-name>.prompt.md`
- [ ] Command: imperative steps with explicit tool invocations
- [ ] Command: references Skills via `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` for domain knowledge
- [ ] Prompt: YAML frontmatter with `mode:`, `description:`, and `tools:`
- [ ] Prompt: delegates to the Command or mirrors its logic
- [ ] Naming: kebab-case, verb (single action) or verb-noun (compound action)
- [ ] Both files exist (cross-tool parity)

**Governing documents:** [STD-TEC-AI-004](../../../../standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-004-workflow-authoring.md) • [GUID-TECH-IMPL-006](./GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md) • [GUID-TECH-IMPL-007](./GUID-TECH-IMPL-007-github-copilot-prompt-authoring-guidance.md) • [PTN-TEC-AI-003](../../../../patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md)
page_texts.41:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#rule-checklist]

#### Rule Checklist

- [ ] Claude rule at `.claude/rules/<concern>.md`
- [ ] Copilot instruction at `.github/instructions/<concern>.instructions.md`
- [ ] Claude frontmatter: `paths:` as YAML list of globs
- [ ] Copilot frontmatter: `applyTo:` as comma-separated glob string
- [ ] Content is directive (imperative language)

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#preparation-steps]

#### Preparation Steps

1. **Identify your intent** — What capability are you trying to add to the AI assistant?
    - Required input: A clear statement of the problem being solved
    - Key activity: Run through the [Construct Selection Decision Tree](#construct-selection-decision-tree)
    - Expected output: Construct type identified, governing documents identified

2. **Read the governing standard** — Skim the mandatory requirements (MR-) sections
    - Required input: Standard document ID from the decision tree
    - Key activity: Focus on MR-1 (file location/naming) and the structure MR
    - Expected output: Understanding of mandatory file structure

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#execution-steps]

#### Execution Steps

1. **Create the file(s) at the correct path**
    - Apply naming conventions from the [Naming Quick-Reference](#naming-quick-reference)
    - Copy the structural template from the relevant guidance document
    - Fill in content following the Detailed Guidance section of the guidance

2. **Create the cross-tool equivalent** (for Commands, Rules, and Instructions)
    - Apply [PTN-TEC-AI-003](../../../../patterns/technology/ai-development/PTN-TEC-AI-003-cross-tool-construct-synchronization-pattern.md) rules
    - Use vendor-native frontmatter keys per [STD-TEC-AI-005](../../../../standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-005-file-pattern-instruction.md)

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#validation-steps]

#### Validation Steps

1. **Run the per-construct checklist** — Every checkbox must pass
    - Required input: Your authored file(s)
    - Key activity: Compare against the relevant [checklist](#per-construct-checklists)
    - Expected output: All items checked; ready for PR

2. **Verify naming compliance** — Ensure names match conventions
    - Required input: File paths and construct names

page_texts.52:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#decision-point-1-skill-vs-command]

#### Decision Point 1: Skill vs. Command

**Context:** You have expertise content that includes both knowledge and procedural steps.
**Options:** (A) Encode everything in a Skill, (B) Split into Skill (knowledge) + Command (procedure)
**Criteria:** Does the content include tool invocations or sequential CLI steps? Does it need to be reused by multiple workflows?
**Recommendation:** If it has tool invocations → Command that references a Skill. If it's pure domain knowledge → Skill only.
page_texts.53:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#decision-point-2-rule-vs-skill]

#### Decision Point 2: Rule vs. Skill

**Context:** You have behavioral guidance specific to certain file types.
**Options:** (A) Create a rule file, (B) Create a Skill
**Criteria:** Is the content < 20 lines? Is it a constraint rather than a procedure? Does it apply to a glob pattern of files?
**Recommendation:** If < 20 lines and constraint-focused → Rule. If > 20 lines or includes workflow → Skill.
page_texts.54:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#decision-point-3-single-construct-vs-cross-tool-pair]

#### Decision Point 3: Single Construct vs. Cross-Tool Pair

**Context:** You're creating a new workflow or rule.
**Options:** (A) Create for one tool only, (B) Create matched pair
**Criteria:** Will both Claude Code and GitHub Copilot users need this capability?
**Recommendation:** Always create matched pairs unless the construct is inherently single-platform (e.g., Claude-only `$ARGUMENTS` handling). See PTN-TEC-AI-003.
page_texts.56:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#recommended-tools]

#### Recommended Tools

| Tool Category | Tool Name | Purpose | Usage Guidelines |
|---|---|---|---|
| Token counting | `tiktoken` (Python) | Verify instruction files < 15k tokens | Run on CLAUDE.md and copilot-instructions.md before commit |
| Sync validation | `/eap-ai-sync` command | Detect desynchronized constructs | Run after creating or modifying any paired construct |
| Linting | `markdownlint` | Validate markdown structure | Included in `task lint` |
| Glob testing | Any glob playground | Verify patterns match intended files | Test `paths:` / `applyTo:` patterns before committing |

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#use-case-1-team-adding-their-first-custom-skill]

#### Use Case 1: Team Adding Their First Custom Skill

**Scenario Description:** A team needs to encode domain knowledge about their Medicaid claims processing rules for AI assistants.
**Context:** No existing Skills cover claims adjudication logic.
**Guidance Application:**
1. Decision tree → "Define reusable domain expertise" → Skill
2. Read STD-001 MR-1 through MR-4
3. Create `.claude/skills/claims-adjudicator/SKILL.md`
4. Apply naming: kebab-case role-noun ✓
5. Run Skill checklist
**Adaptations:** Domain-specific workflow steps reference the team's internal documentation.
**Success Factors:** Skill stays focused on claims domain; delegates implementation to the team's engineering process (or a repository-defined implementation Skill, if one exists).
page_texts.60:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#use-case-2-platform-team-creating-a-new-devops-workflow]

#### Use Case 2: Platform Team Creating a New DevOps Workflow

**Scenario Description:** Platform engineering needs a "deploy canary" workflow available in both tools.
**Context:** The workflow involves multiple steps (build, push image, deploy canary, validate, promote).
**Guidance Application:**
1. Decision tree → "Multi-step workflow triggered by user" → "For both" → Command + Prompt pair
2. Read STD-004 + GUID-006 + GUID-007
3. Create `.claude/commands/deploy-canary.md` (source of truth)
4. Create `.github/prompts/deploy-canary.prompt.md` (derived)
5. Naming: verb-noun ✓
6. Run Command + Prompt checklist
**Adaptations:** Command references a repository-defined IaC-expertise Skill (e.g., a `deployer` Skill in repositories that maintain one) — `eap-ref-architecture` does not currently define one; deployment automation for its own tooling (e.g., `.github/workflows/deploy-ai-gov-review-svc.yml`, `.tooling/components/`) is handled directly by Commands/scripts rather than a dedicated Skill.
**Success Factors:** Both tools provide equivalent capability; PTN-003 parity maintained.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#use-case-3-adding-file-pattern-rules-for-a-new-language]

#### Use Case 3: Adding File-Pattern Rules for a New Language

**Scenario Description:** Team is onboarding a Go component and needs AI assistants to follow Go conventions when editing `.go` files.
**Context:** No existing rules cover Go; content is brief (12 lines of conventions).
**Guidance Application:**
1. Decision tree → "Behavioral constraints scoped to file patterns" → Rule
2. Read STD-005 + GUID-008
3. Create `.claude/rules/golang.md` with `paths: ['**/*.go']`
4. Create `.github/instructions/golang.instructions.md` with `applyTo: '**/*.go'`
5. Run Rule checklist — content is 12 lines ✓, no workflow steps ✓
**Adaptations:** None needed.
**Success Factors:** Both files have equivalent content with vendor-native frontmatter.

[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#governance-structure]

#### Governance Structure

- **Decision authority:** Individual authors create constructs; EA Practice reviews for standards conformance
- **Oversight:** PRs to repositories containing AI constructs require EA review when modifying Skills, Agents, or Instruction files
- **Exception handling:** Non-conformant constructs discovered post-merge are logged as tech debt and tracked for remediation
- **Review cycle:** This quick-start guide is updated when new standards or construct types are introduced
page_texts.65:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#governance-integration]

#### Governance Integration

All constructs authored using this quick-start guide are subject to the same governance as any other enterprise architecture artifact. EA review validates conformance to the applicable standard(s) identified in the decision tree.

> **AI Risk Classification:** Constructs that interact with PHI, eligibility determinations, claims data, or clinical outputs may be subject to elevated governance obligations beyond EA standards conformance. Refer to [GUID-SEC-AI-GOV-2.9.06](../../../guidance/security/GUID-SEC-AI-GOV-2.9.06-ai-risk-classification.md) for risk-tiered requirements including ethics review, bias testing, and executive approval applicable to high-risk AI systems.
page_texts.67:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#validation-approaches]

#### Validation Approaches

- **Self-validation:** Authors use per-construct checklists before PR submission
- **Peer validation:** Team members familiar with AI constructs review naming and structure
- **EA validation:** Enterprise Architecture Practice reviews for standards conformance and cross-reference completeness
- **Automated validation:** CI pipelines check for file naming violations and missing cross-tool pairs (where implemented)
page_texts.69:
[strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-011-ai-construct-authoring-quick-start.md#risk-assessment]

#### Risk Assessment

| Risk Category | Risk Description | Probability | Impact | Mitigation Strategy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Construct misclassification | Author selects wrong construct type | Medium | Medium | Decision tree + PR review |
| Naming drift | Teams invent non-standard naming | Medium | High | Checklist enforcement + CI linting |
| Cross-tool desync | One tool's construct updated without the other | High | Medium | PTN-003 + `/eap-ai-sync` workflow |
| Stale quick-start | New standards added without updating this guide | Low | High | Change history tracks standard additions |
